HOST A WEBSITE ON AMAZON S3

By
Emmanuel Aidoo
September 2026

Introducing Today's Project!

Project overview

In this project, I will demonstrate how to host a static website using Amazon S3
by creating an S3 bucket, uploading website ﬁles (HTML and images),
conﬁguring static website hosting, and managing public access settings. I'm
doing this project to learn the fundamentals of cloud storage and web hosting on
AWS, as part of building out my cloud portfolio.

Tools and concepts

The key service I used in this project is Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service) for
cloud storage and static web hosting. Key concepts I learned include creating
globally unique S3 buckets, uploading and managing web assets like HTML ﬁles
and images, conﬁguring static website hosting endpoints, managing object-level
access permissions via Access Control Lists (ACLs), and utilizing JSON-based
bucket policies to enforce granular security controls such as preventing
accidental object deletion.

Time, challenges, and wins

This project took me approximately 45 minutes to complete. The most
challenging part was troubleshooting the initial 403 Forbidden error and
understanding how private object settings interact with static website hosting. It
was most rewarding to see my static HTML ﬁle and images successfully render
into a live, publicly accessible website hosted entirely in the cloud on AWS S3!

How I Set Up an S3 Bucket

What I did in this step

In this step, I will create a new S3 bucket with a globally unique name because I
need a designated storage space in the cloud to hold all the ﬁles and assets
required for my website.

How long it took to create the bucket

Creating an S3 bucket took me around 2 to 3 minutes because it only required
logging into the AWS console, navigating to Amazon S3, entering a unique bucket
name, and keeping the default conﬁguration settings.

Understanding bucket name uniqueness

S3 bucket names are globally unique because all AWS accounts share a single,
global namespace. This means that once you create a bucket name, no other
AWS account in the entire world can use that exact same name until your bucket
is deleted.

Upload Website Files to S3

What I did in this step

In this step, I will download the required website assets and upload them into my
S3 bucket because an S3 bucket needs actual ﬁles like HTML code and images
to display a fully functional web page.

Files I uploaded

I uploaded two ﬁles to my S3 bucket—they were the index.html blueprint ﬁle and
the zipped folder of image assets (NextWork - Everyone...love_ﬁles.zip)
containing the pictures for my website.

How the files work together

Both ﬁles are necessary for this project because the index.html ﬁle acts as the
webpage blueprint containing the text and structure, while the image folder
supplies the actual visual assets and media that the HTML code references to
display pictures on the website.

Static Website Hosting on S3

What I did in this step

In this step, I will conﬁgure static website hosting in the properties of my S3
bucket because this tells AWS to generate a public endpoint URL that renders my
uploaded HTML ﬁle as a web page on the internet.

Understanding website hosting

Website hosting means storing website ﬁles on a server and assigning them a
public URL so that anyone on the internet can access and view your web pages,
rather than keeping the ﬁles restricted locally on your own computer.

How I enabled website hosting

To enable website hosting with my S3 bucket, I navigated to the Properties tab of
my bucket, scrolled down to the Static website hosting section, clicked Edit,
enabled the feature, set the hosting type to "Host a static website," speciﬁed
index.html as the index document, and saved the changes to generate my public
website endpoint URL.

Access Control Lists (ACLs)

An ACL (Access Control List) is a set of rules that determines who can access
and manage speciﬁc objects within a storage bucket. I enabled ACLs in this
setup so I can control access permissions for individual website ﬁles and objects.

Bucket Endpoints

Understanding bucket endpoint URLs

Once static website hosting is enabled, S3 produces a public website endpoint
URL that points directly to your web server. It uses the bucket's name and AWS
Region to generate a web link.

What I saw when I tested the endpoint

When I ﬁrst visited the bucket endpoint URL, I saw a 403 Forbidden error
message. The reason for this error was that although static website hosting was
enabled, the ﬁles (index.html and the image folder) inside the S3 bucket were still
private by default, meaning public access was not yet permitted.

Success!

What I did in this step

In this step, I will update the permissions of my uploaded S3 objects to public
using ACLs because S3 objects are private by default, and making them public
allows visitors all over the world to view the website without getting error
messages.

How I resolved the 403 error

To resolve this 403 Forbidden error, I selected the uploaded ﬁles inside my S3
bucket and updated their access permissions to public using Access Control
Lists (ACLs), which granted internet visitors the required permission to read and
view the website ﬁles.

Bucket Policies

What I did in this extension

In this project extension I'm about to control acess to my bucket using bucket
policies I'm doing this so that i can control who csn delete my ﬁles

Understanding bucket policies

An alternative to ACLs are bucket policies, which are policies that controls access
to objects in our bucket The beneﬁt of using bucket policies is to control how we
want our object to be access in a bucket while ACLs are useful for contol access
to speciﬁc objects in our bucket

What my bucket policy does

My bucket policy denies everyone form deleting the objects in my bucket I
tested this by trying to delete the index.html object form my bucket and saw an
error message preventing me form deleting the object
